title: Carrying a tool that runs out
target: How to plan around R.E.P.O. gear that discharges or wears out, given that different tools fail in different ways.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Spare batteries or a charging station
A route you intend to finish

steps.do: Work out which of your gear uses battery before you set out.
steps.because: tools such as the leaf blower carry a drain rate of their own (batteryDrainRate)

steps.do: Expect hitting something to cost more charge than using a tool as intended.
steps.because: the leaf blower drains separately when it hits a monster (batteryDrainOnEnemyHit)

steps.do: Watch gear that wears out as well as gear that runs down.
steps.because: melee weapons drain durability when they hit (durabilityDrainOnEnemiesAndPVP)

steps.do: Carry spares rather than relying on one item.
steps.because: batteries are carried items rather than a shared pool (ItemBattery)

steps.do: Leave a charging station where you will come back through it.
steps.because: the charging station is an object you place (ChargingStation)

commonMistakes: Setting out with no spare battery.
Using a tool as a weapon and being surprised by the drain.
Never checking a melee weapon after a fight.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
